verdicts.evidence: Opened the publish dialog on base (installed bundle 0.5.22) without publishing. Five destinations, and exactly two carry a "The gate" tag - "Push to an OCI repository" and "Put the reviewed packet on the repository", which the dialog names as the same distribution boundary reached by the two routes this Studio has. "Load into this Rancher" and "Push the source to GitHub" both read "No sign-off", and the catalog row is "Both + extensions team" and explicitly not tickable. Both gate rows were refused with `barn-publish-gate-oci` / `-repository` reading "This change has never been handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it." distributionGate() in review.ts is the single enforcement point and it is only consulted by the two gate rows.

Drove /barn/editor, /barn/extensions/base/files, /barn/extensions/base/review, /barn/extensions/base/build-failed and /barn/extensions/base/verification: no approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control on any of them. Typed into the pod terminal (`echo barn-w4-cli-check` echoed back) with nobody asked. The publish dialog labels the local load and the GitHub source push "No sign-off" and states "Loading this into a Rancher to try it, or handing it over on GitHub to ask for a review, needs nobody." Settings goes further: settings-signoff-enforcement says the sign-off matrix records intent only, and "a developer load reaches only this Rancher and is ungated" is fixed in code, with the publish dialog naming any stored value it is not obeying (I saw it do exactly that: "Settings put an outcome sign-off at 'Notified'. The gate takes both regardless").

The publish dialog carries a SIGN-OFFS section with both rows ("Code review - Is it safe?" and "Outcome sign-off - Does it do the job?", both "Not signed off yet") and both gate destinations were refused. distributionGate() requires code and outcome to be verdict 'approved' AND to cover the packet (covers() via sameCommit), refusing at 'no-brief', 'no-packet', 'stale-packet', 'changes-requested', 'awaiting-code', 'awaiting-outcome' and 'same-signer' before it will answer 'open'. The confirm button read "Pick a destination" and was disabled, and the footer said "Nothing is ticked, so nothing will be published." The positive half (approve both, then the same publish proceeds) could not be exercised: creating a packet needs a hand-over to GitHub and the barn-settings Secret holds no token, so no packet exists to sign against. Judged on the enforcement, which is what the rule is about, and which holds.

The two records are separate objects: review.json's signoffs.code (written by signCodeReview on screen 12) and signoffs.outcome (signOutcome on screen 13), each carrying its own principal, name, at and sha, and neither write touches the other. The publish dialog draws them as two rows with two different questions and a note that "Two people answer two questions". distributionGate() has an explicit 'same-signer' refusal that fires when code.principal === outcome.principal, with the reason "one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice". Confirmed against the live barn-review-base ConfigMap, whose signoffs object is keyed code/outcome.

review.ts:945 packetPullRequest() now exists and does the right thing: it answers from the packet record first (state 'recorded'), only asks GitHub about packet.branch, and has a 'no-packet' state whose sentence is "This has never been handed over, so there is no pull request to be its record yet." But `grep -rn packetPullRequest pkg/barn` finds no caller outside its own definition. Screen 12 still runs the old checkPullRequest() at review-change.vue:1644, which reads `this.branch = branches?.current` and calls findOpenPullRequest(extension, repo, this.branch). Driving /barn/review/base/working in the installed bundle, the chip read "No GitHub token" with the title "No GitHub token is configured, so nothing can be asked. Opens the editor settings." - the token state, not the hand-over state, and clicking it opened EditorSettingsModal rather than a PR.
verdicts.defect: packetPullRequest() has landed but nothing calls it, so the fix is dead code and screen 12 is unchanged. review-change.vue:1644 checkPullRequest() still searches GitHub for an open PR whose head is listBranches().current; a packet's branch is made with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so that branch is never the packet's. The visible consequence on base (never handed over) is a chip saying "No GitHub token" where packetPullRequest() would say "This has never been handed over, so there is no pull request to be its record yet" - the accurate answer, and one that needs no token. The change is to import packetPullRequest from review.ts and drive prState/pr from its six states instead of the four checkPullRequest computes. Secondary and unchanged: with no token in the barn-settings Secret and no repository remembered, the hand-over refuses before it reaches GitHub, so no queue entry backed by a real PR can be produced in this environment.

verdicts.evidence: review.ts:1051 handedOverExtensions() now exists and answers exactly the queue's question (one ConfigMap read per extension, in parallel, an extension with no packets is not handed over). `grep -rn handedOverExtensions pkg/barn` finds no caller outside its own definition. review-queue.vue's load() (line 368) still does `const summaries = await listExtensions()` and then `enrich()` on every one of them. Driving /barn/review in the installed bundle: base - whose barn-review-base ConfigMap has `"packets": {}` and which has never been handed over - is a row in the queue, the header reads "Waiting on you 1", and the row itself says "Never handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it. It is still the author's own working tree." So "work for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue" still does not hold.
verdicts.defect: handedOverExtensions() has landed but nothing calls it. review-queue.vue:368 load() still enumerates every extension from listExtensions() and enriches each, so an author's dirty working tree is a row in somebody else's queue and counts toward "Waiting on you". The row explains itself in words and carries a queue-not-handed chip, which is honest, but a row that explains why it should not be there is still a row. The change is to filter `summaries` through handedOverExtensions(names) before mapping them into this.rows.

verdicts.evidence: Every diff on the review surfaces is one `git diff <baseline>` (BASELINE_SH in extensions.ts resolves refs/barn/published/oci, then refs/barn/published/local, then HEAD), so intermediate commits collapse by construction. Demonstrated on base: verify-w2-review.txt was added and then removed across the intermediate commits 2abd586..24b3922, and it appears nowhere in the whole-change reading (4 files: HARNESS.md, product.ts, verify-w4-workspace.txt, w4-review.generated.ts) - only the net state is shown. Measuring from 2abd586 instead (?from=2abd586) brings it back as "deleted -1", which is the same collapse taken from a different point. Screen 04 says the same thing in words: "Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree." One caveat: screen 12 does not read baselineRef(), so its scope notice says "measured from the last published version" even on base, where nothing has ever been published and the baseline is really HEAD. Screen 04 does read baselineRef and says which point it used.

Both halves of the path are wired and the capture half was verified live this wave. The brief travels: screen 12's header on base renders WHAT THIS IS FOR / WHO HAS IT / WHAT CHANGES FOR THEM / WHAT WE ARE DELIBERATELY NOT DOING read out of the extension's own BRIEF.md, with a line saying which section each came from. The capture: I sent a comment from screen 12 to the assistant and then read the pod's own turn log (`node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs turns 5`), which had recorded it as turn tmt67wfq06176y with the full prompt, screen "review-comment", principal local://user-btc48 and who "Default Admin" - and had separately recorded the line I typed straight into the terminal with an empty screen, which is the honest distinction. The review half renders per hunk: each hunk carried its own strip, here in the unrecorded state ("4 lines changed in the pod, no prompt recorded") with a summary "No prompt recorded for any of this change's 8 lines". A hunk carrying a real prompt could not be produced in this environment: claude has no credentials in any of the three pods ("Not logged in - Please run /login"), so no turn ends in a commit, `commit` is "" on every recorded turn, and no commit anywhere carries a Barn-Turn trailer for provenanceFor() to blame a line back to.

Both halves now work, driven against the installed bundle. changedFilesSince/fileDiffSince (extensions.ts:2505, :2527) take an arbitrary commit, and screen 12 uses them for both the list and the patch. /barn/review/base/working?scope=since&from=2abd586 narrowed to 5 files with an info banner "Showing what has landed since 2abd586, the commit your approval was given against: 5 files. The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 4 files. Approve still commits all of it." The narrowed list is genuinely a different measurement, not a subset: it contains verify-w2-review.txt as "deleted -1", a file absent from the 4-file whole-change reading, and selecting it rendered its deletion patch, so the diff moves with the list. Toggling the chip with no ?from used the recorded look (24b3922) and said so. Refusal is real rather than a silent fallback: ?from=deadbeef...(40 hex, not a commit) put the chip in error tone and rendered rc-scope-refused - "...it could not be measured: deadbeef... is not a commit in base any more, so there is nothing to measure from. The whole change is shown instead, and nothing has been hidden from you." The queue side is wired to it: review-queue.vue's openSince() opens the same route with scope=since and from set to the commit the approval was given against.

Both amber routes end in the same workspace. Build failure: seeded barn.publish.failure and loaded /barn/extensions/base/build-failed - the card carries barn-to-workspace "Back to the workspace" and the apply-fix and roll-back actions all sit on that one panel rather than routing anywhere new. Rejected review: review-change.vue's requestChanges() (line ~1624) and its send-comment handler (line ~1501) both `$router.push({ name: EDITOR_ROUTE, params: { extension }, query: { tab: 'terminal' } })`, and I saw the send do it - the page left .rc__body immediately after "Send to the assistant" landed. Screen 13's hand-back does the same, and its own panel carries "Back to the workspace". No separate remediation surface exists anywhere in pages/.

Verified end to end this wave. Commented on hunk 26 of product.ts on screen 12 with "w4-cross probe: rename this variable to nodeConditionTrend (verifier w4-cross-screen)" and pressed Send to the assistant. The barn-review-base ConfigMap recorded the comment with sentAt 2026-08-23T19:46:05.786Z and sentHow "sent", and `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor` in the pod shows it arrived verbatim, wrapped as a reviewer instruction: "A reviewer looked at this change and asked for something. It is about pages/Home.vue around line 10. Their words: w4-cross probe: rename this variable to nodeConditionTrend (verifier w4-cross-screen). Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did." The reviewer wrote no code, and the author still approves: the assistant answered "Not logged in - Please run /login" and changed nothing. Screen 12 also offers rc-comment-record-N (record without sending) beside rc-comment-send-N, so sending is a deliberate second act.

The guarantee now holds and the point is durable. The sessionStorage record is gone: publishExtension writes refs/barn/working-build via recordBaseline at the moment a build has installed (extensions.ts:2197, :4082), lastWorkingBuild reads it back out of the pod, and readWorkingBuild is what BuildFailure.findWayBack reaches for first. I proved the write mechanism actually works in the pod rather than trusting it: ran recordBaseline's exact shell by hand in barn-base-extension against a scratch ref (GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree, add -A, write-tree, commit-tree -p HEAD, update-ref) - it produced 244643c, `git log -1 --format='%H%x1f%s%x1f%cr'` returned exactly what lastWorkingBuild parses, and neither HEAD nor the index moved. I deleted the ref and the root-owned .git/refs/barn it left behind. findWayBack has four tiers and always lands on one, and it says which it landed on rather than implying the best case: on base, which has never been published, screen 08 offered an enabled "Roll back to the snapshot 'autosave 1932 on Aug 23'" (taken 2 minutes earlier by EditorMasthead.autoSnapshot, which fingerprints the working diff and snapshots when it moves) with the note "no build of this extension has succeeded here yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a build that is known to have worked". So the design's "snapshot taken before the change that breaks it" exists in practice via the autosave, and the durable ref is the better point when a build has actually succeeded. The exec fix is what makes this real: createSnapshot now verifies its tag afterwards instead of sending git tag to /dev/null, and the pod has four live barn-snap tags. I did not click Roll back - it would have destroyed four other verifiers' uncommitted work in the shared base pod - so "rolling back returns the workspace to it" is read off the code (restoreSnapshot, and the panel refusing when the safety snapshot cannot be taken) rather than observed.

The overflow menu on each row of /barn/extensions carries "Remove the local install". On nodehealth, which is installed (the row reads "catalog - v0.1.0" and a UIPlugin nodehealth 0.1.0 exists in the cluster), the item read "Remove the local install v0.1.0" and was enabled. On base and demo, neither of which is installed, the same item read "Remove the local install not installed" and was disabled, so it tracks the real UIPlugin rather than being decorative. The publish dialog states the same contract from the other end: "Reversible: 'Remove local install' takes it back off." I did not click it - uninstalling nodehealth would have pulled it out from under the other verifiers.

The create route passes through the brief. new-extension.vue's create() calls ensureExtension() and then pushes BRIEF_ROUTE with the prompt, outcome and placement in the query (line 229) - there is no path from screen 02 to the workspace that skips it. brief.vue's agree() then pushes EDITOR_ROUTE with query brief=1, which the workspace picks up and sends to the assistant as the session's first instruction (line 1181). So 02 -> 10 -> 03, which is the flow map's green run. By contrast screen 04 is only reachable from a "Review N changes" affordance and nothing routes through it. Both screens render in the installed bundle (/barn/extensions/new and /barn/extensions/base/brief). Two caveats stated rather than buried: the brief screen carries a ghost "Skip the brief" button that pushes EDITOR_ROUTE directly (brief.vue:1192), so the stage is on the path but not unskippable - though distributionGate() then refuses at 'no-brief', so skipping only defers it to the gate; and the import path (onImported) lands on the studio home rather than the brief, which is a different entry from the flow map's "describe what you want". I did not create an extension to watch the route run, because that provisions another pod into the shared namespace.

Read base's BRIEF.md in the pod: "## How we will know it worked" lists four items, two ticked. /barn/extensions/base/verification lists those same four items in the same order, as the checklist, with the two ticked ones showing "evidence captured" and the other two "not measured" - nothing is re-entered on screen 13 and nothing is invented. Screen 12 shows the same four under "DOES IT DO THE JOB? 4 criteria", so one authored list feeds both. Screen 13 also frames it correctly ("You are checking whether this does the job, not whether the code is any good") and each criterion has Yes / No / Can't tell plus "Show me", walked against the live preview pane on the right, and the note says recording the result ticks the boxes back into BRIEF.md.

Half of this closed this wave and half did not, so it is worth being precise. The two resolutions now exist and both work. I added a line containing "alerting" to base's working tree (verify-w4-cross.txt) - a word base's brief lists under what it is deliberately not doing - and screen 13's Scope card moved from "Nothing this change adds mentions monitoring/alerting/history/... " to a drift row naming the term and the file, with verify-accept-drift-alerting ("That is fine - add it to the brief") and verify-remove-drift-alerting ("Remove it") beside it. Clicking accept rewrote BRIEF.md for real - the non-goals line moved into "What changes for them" stamped "(accepted during verification on 2026-08-23 by admin)" - and the warning went. removeDrift is wired to askAssistant with the term, the files and an instruction not to touch BRIEF.md; I did not fire it into the shared pod. I restored BRIEF.md from my backup and removed the probe file afterwards.
verdicts.defect: The detection is still the half that does not hold. scopeDrift() is a word match: it takes up to six terms out of the brief's "What we are deliberately not doing" section and looks for them in the change's added lines. So work that is outside the brief but does not happen to reuse one of those words is not flagged at all, and an extension whose brief has no non-goals section gets "there is nothing to measure the change against" rather than a comparison. The design's clause is "the build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged", which a term match over one section cannot deliver. Second, smaller: accepting one term accepts the whole sentence it was found in. base's non-goals were "No alerting, and no history beyond 24 hours. Both belong in monitoring." - accepting "alerting" moved that entire sentence out, leaving the section as "_not stated_", so the untouched non-goal about 24-hour history was silently accepted too and every later scope check on that extension answers "nothing to measure against".

verdicts.evidence: base has four changed files in its pod and a live preview rendering in the workspace's right pane, and it is not installed anywhere: the only UIPlugins in the cluster are barn 0.5.22 and nodehealth 0.1.0, and the home row's "Remove the local install" is disabled with "not installed". So nothing about working in the preview has published anything. The line is drawn in words too, in three places: the workspace says "2 changes - Only you can see them. Nothing is asked of you until you publish", screen 04 says "Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree", and the publish dialog says every destination is a separate choice with none ticked. Snapshotted per build is the autosave in EditorMasthead (four barn-snap tags in the pod, the newest 2 minutes old when I looked).

Re-checked both halves against the installed bundle; neither has changed. The settings page's permission card is explicit that there is nothing to change: "Not settable, and not per user. The pod starts claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions (pod/claude-session.sh), so this is the level in force for everybody... a level chosen here would be undone within seconds". The workspace strip shows barn-permission-chip reading "Edits apply without asking", which is a statement, not the control the design draws. And a second surface still edits the GitHub token: I clicked the "No GitHub token" chip on screen 12 and EditorSettingsModal opened with a single password field placeholder ghp_..., titled "Connect GitHub", with an "All Studio settings" link back to screen 09. It is reachable from screens 02, 03 and 12.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged from the previous wave. (1) The permission mode is not a control on either screen, so it cannot be changed in one place and seen in the other, and the design's "the permission mode as a real control" on screen 03 does not exist. The settings page is honest about why, which is right, but honesty is not the promise. (2) components/EditorSettingsModal.vue still stores and removes the GitHub token and is opened from screens 02, 03 and 12; it shares studio-settings.ts with the settings page so the two cannot disagree, and it deliberately offers only the credential, but screen 09's caption has it replacing the token modal outright.

verdicts.evidence: Four of the five named capabilities are intact and were driven, not just found. CLI: the workspace's Terminal tab attached a live xterm to the pod's tmux session over the exec subresource - I typed `echo barn-w4-cli-check`, saw it echo, and saw claude's own footer ("bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)"). Files: /barn/extensions/base/files renders the tree, ten history entries and an editable pane. GitHub import: the Import dialog does connection as step one, and with no token stored step two degrades correctly to "name the repository below or paste its URL - a public one clones with no token at all", with step three offering branch and name and no link out to settings. Settings: /barn/settings renders connection, permissions, access and data with live values. Publish: the dialog reads the version and changeset out of the pod and runs the pre-flight checks ("Scanned 4 files for tokens, keys and kubeconfigs"); I did not publish. The strict write path through the new exec layer also works from the UI - screen 13's accept-drift wrote BRIEF.md into the pod and I saw the file change. probe-errors.mjs reports ALL CLEAN across all ten screens. What is broken is the raw-output surface this rule names, see the defect.
verdicts.defect: The "Show raw output" strip on screen 03 - the control that exists to make good on "the raw terminal output is still there, one click away" - is broken in the installed bundle. One click opens it and it renders "the dev server's log could not be read: HTTP 406" with "The last 0 of them." The cause is one header on a function added this wave: devServerLog (extensions.ts:4369) fetches the pod log with `{ headers: { Accept: 'text/plain' } }`, and the apiserver behind Rancher's proxy refuses that - "only the following media types are accepted: application/json, application/yaml, application/vnd.kube...". I proved it from the page: the same URL returns 406 with Accept: text/plain and 200 with the log body with no Accept header or with */*. Dropping the header is the fix. Scope, so this is not over-read: no capability of the current build was lost - claude's own raw stream is still one click away on the Terminal tab and works, and it is the dev server's log, not the assistant's, that this strip serves. But the control the redesign put on screen 03 for this clause errors on its first click, and it regressed in the same wave that changed the exec and fetch layer.

verdicts.evidence: Re-checked, unchanged. `grep -rn "from '@shell|from '@components|from '@rancher"` over pkg/barn finds Rancher components in only five files, none of which is one of the ten screens: ExtensionFiles, ExtensionSelect, NewExtensionModal, PublishStatus and PublishSplit. Every screen is drawn with components/ui's own SBadge, SBanner, SButton, SCard, SChip, SEmpty, SField, SIcon, SLabel, SMenu, SModal, SPanel, SRow, STabs, SToolbar. SortableTable appears nowhere in the package. I dumped screen 01's rendered markup and it is a div grid - `<div class="studio-home__table"><div class="studio-home__head"><button class="studio-home__th" aria-sort="none">` - not a table element and not the Clusters page's SortableTable.
verdicts.defect: The Studio is built almost entirely on its own primitives, so Banner, Card, Tabbed and SortableTable are all reimplementations, and screen 01 in particular is a hand-rolled div table with its own sort buttons rather than the SortableTable pattern the rationale names (27:5, 27:91). The reimplementations are competent and the sort affordances work; the rule is about not needing new primitives, and the product needed fifteen.
